original_question: In the polynomial intertwining construction, does the resulting polynomial vary continuously with P2?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Question 11 of Ben Bielefeld's Questions in Quasiconformal Surgery: "Does the resulting polynomial vary continuously in P2?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right construction (intertwining, not mating or tuning), the right output object (the polynomial produced by the surgery), and the right variable of dependence (P2). It is already very close to the paper's own wording in Question 11.
missing_details: The paper's term is "intertwining surgery" (or "an intertwining construction"), not just a generic "polynomial intertwining construction."
P1 is assumed to be a monic polynomial with connected Julia set.
P1 must have a repelling fixed point x0 at which an external ray lands, with combinatorial rotation number p/q.
The construction cuts the dynamical plane of P1 along the q forward images of that ray, producing q disjoint wedges.
P2 is assumed to be a monic polynomial with a ray of the same combinatorial rotation number landing on a repelling periodic point of period dividing q.
The P2 dynamical plane is slit along the corresponding rays, the wedges from P1 are inserted, and the map is adjusted near inverse images of the cut rays to make it continuous.

The continuity question concerns the polynomial obtained from this intertwining only in cases where the construction actually yields something conjugate to a polynomial; that existence issue is separately asked in Question 9.
To make the question stand alone, one should indicate that P1 and the chosen ray/combinatorial data are being held fixed while P2 varies.
The paper leaves the topology/parameter-space meaning of "vary continuously" implicit, so a fully stand-alone reformulation should preserve that this notion is not further specified there.

The nearby context notes that the outlined construction is intended for the case where the relevant rays in the P2 space land at a repelling orbit, and it "doesn't seem to work" when they land at a parabolic orbit.
refined_question: Fix a monic polynomial P1 with connected Julia set and a repelling fixed point x0 such that an external ray of combinatorial rotation number p/q lands at x0. Cut the dynamical plane of P1 along the q forward images of that ray to obtain q wedges, and perform the intertwining surgery with a monic polynomial P2 that has a ray of the same combinatorial rotation number landing on a repelling periodic point whose period divides q, by slitting the P2 plane along the corresponding rays, inserting those wedges, and adjusting the map near inverse images of the cut rays to make it continuous. In the cases where this intertwining construction yields a map conjugate to a polynomial, does the resulting polynomial depend continuously on P2?
justification: The draft is targeting the third surgery type in Section 1, namely intertwining surgery. After defining that construction for a fixed P1 and an admissible P2 via matching rays and combinatorial rotation number, the paper asks exactly Question 11: whether the resulting polynomial varies continuously in P2. This is the nearest official formulation. The draft is therefore essentially correct, but it omits the hypotheses defining the intertwining setup and the tacit dependence on Question 9, which asks when the construction actually gives something conjugate to a polynomial. The analogous continuity question for tuning appears earlier as Question 6, so the word "intertwining" makes Question 11 the correct target.
